holding_summary: The court held that a tenant who holds over after the expiration of a lease becomes bound, at the landlord's election, as tenant for another year on the prior lease's terms, and that this rule applies even where the holding over stems from circumstances beyond the tenant's convenience, such as an ill boarder who could not safely be moved.

quotes.text: This court held in Commissioners of Pilots v. Clark, 33 N. Y.,, 251, that the rule is too well settled to be disputed that where a tenant holds over after the expiration of his term the law will imply an agreement to hold for a year upon the terms of the prior lease; that the option to so regard it is with the landlord and not with the tenant; and that the latter holds over his term at his peril.

Defendant’s lease ended, by its terms, on May 1, and provided that the premises should be occupied as a private dwelling and not sublet without the written consent of the lessor. Defendant sublet the premises to C., who occupied them as a boarding house, and one of her boarders was a chronic invalid.

notes: Boarding-house subletting appears only as the tenant's breach of a 'private dwelling'/no-sublet covenant and the source of the holdover delay; the court does not otherwise characterize the sub-tenancy's legal type (lease/license/lodging), so characterization is left null. who_was_letting/duration reflect the sub-tenant Mrs. Coventry's boarding-house operation, whose boarders' occupancy length is not stated.

court: New York Court of Common Pleas, General Term
holding_summary: Where a boarding-house keeper sues to enforce his statutory lien on a boarder's baggage after the boarder clandestinely removed it to avoid paying his board bill, the action is one for wrongful conversion of personal property within subdivision 2 of Code of Civil Procedure §2895, so the justice must include in the judgment the defendant's liability to arrest on execution.

quotes.text: That the plaintiff was a boarding-house keeper in the city of Hew York) that the defendant was a boarder, occupying a room and taking .his breakfast with plaintiff; that defendant, after becoming indebted to plaintiff, clandestinely left the house unknown to plaintiff or his family, and in a secret manner removed all his baggage and wardrobe, except an old pair of pants and a vest.

where, as in this case, the cause of action is for the wrongful conversion of personal property, the same is one of the actions specified in subd. 2 of § 2895 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and consequently the justice was bound to insert in the judgment the liability of the defendant to arrest upon execution.

Plaintiff claimed a lien against the defendant’s baggage and wardrobe not in actual use under the law giving boarding-house keepers a lien upon all baggage and personal effects of their boarders for unpaid board.
